newsitem.title: GERMANY: Horlick says was suspended from MGAM on "hearsay".
newsitem.headline: Horlick says was suspended from MGAM on "hearsay".

text.p: Nicola Horlick, former head of British pension fund business at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Asset Management, arrived at Frankfurt Airport on Friday saying she had been suspended from MGAM on the basis of "hearsay".

"There has been a very large misunderstanding, they should have asked me, they decided to suspend me on the basis of hearsay. That is appalling. I am sorry, I am not going to be treated like this," Horlick told reporters.

Horlick was suspended earlier this week pending the outcome of an internal investigation into what Deutsche Morgan Grenfell described as "a potential breach of her contract" and Horlick resigned on Thursday.

Horlick went on to say: "It has blown up into the most ridiculous scandal. I have done nothing wrong. Everything I have done has been aimed at keeping my business deals going. Everything I have done is in the best interests of my clients."

She also said that the furore had its roots in what she called "the Peter Young affair" and said that Robert Smith, MGAM's chief executive, had done a "wonderful job" at satisfying regulators, "but there are many people in the organisation who were dissatisfied and thought that more should be done."
Asked what she would do if Deutsche Bank refused to speak to her, Horlick said: "Fly home."
